text:
anya: onboarding note — brought Kestrel9b (Mistral-ish) up on Dedicated. Ran int4 conversion with headwise rotary alpha bake + proj-order packing. QA/rerank evals show scores collapse after ~100-150 tokens, outputs get fragmented and rerank ordering is wrong. dropping quick repro + logs.

sam: can you paste the eval command and one failing example?

anya: repro command:
```
./eval/run_eval.sh --model kestrel9b-int4h --suite rerank,qa --bs 16 --seed 11
```
bad snippet (truncated):
"""
Q: What's next step for duplicate charge?
Expected: ask for last 4 digits, initiate refund, owner=billing
Observed: repeats fragments, suggests wrong owner, low factuality
"""

dmitri: did you test fp16 or int4 without headwise pack to isolate fusion vs quant?

anya: yes — fp16 and int4 per-channel (no headwise pack) are fine. Issue appears only when we do headwise concat + bake rotary alpha into quantized weights AND apply proj-order packing.

nick: so multiple levers: (A) headwise pack + per-head scale quantization, (B) baking rotary alpha into weights (quantized), (C) proj-order re-packing. Which of these reproduces if toggled?

anya: quick ablation:
- int4 (no pack, alpha runtime): baseline-like
- int4h (headwise pack, alpha runtime): small diff
- int4h (headwise + alpha baked): big diff
- int4h + proj-repack + alpha baked: worst

sam: that points to alpha-bake amplification. Could be quantizing alpha (sine/cos multiplier) introduces phase bias per head causing attention phase drift. Also check tokenizer normalization — unicode normalizer mismatch can cause kv-cache indices to shift later on.

anya: I diffed tokens on a failing long thread. Short prefix tokens aligned, but later there is a single id bump around an emoji/soft-hyphen. Example:
```
# fp16 tokens: ... 5012  44  777  999  2
# int4h baked:   ... 5012  44  777 1000  2   <- 999->1000 at ZWJ/soft-hyphen
```
This plus baked-alpha seems to compound.

dmitri: good find. Can you run two quick runtime overrides: (1) force ROTARY_ALPHA_RUNTIME=1 (dont bake alpha), (2) force PROJ_READ_MODE=SOURCE (disable runtime reorder) and measure next-token logits L2 on first 64 tokens vs fp16?

anya: running now. cmds:
```
export REDWOOD_RUNTIME_FLAGS=ROTARY_ALPHA_RUNTIME=1
./serve_local.sh --model kestrel9b-int4h --port 9180 --no-autobatch
```
ci-bot: deploy-check: port 9180 up, health OK, p95 95ms, queued eval.

anya: results: with ROTARY_ALPHA_RUNTIME=1 mean L2 (next-token logits first 64) drops from ~9.8e-3 to ~2.7e-3 and rerank P@1 improves by ~6 points. So alpha bake is a large factor.

sam: next run with PROJ_READ_MODE=SOURCE?

anya: yep:
```
export REDWOOD_RUNTIME_FLAGS=PROJ_READ_MODE=SOURCE
./serve_local.sh --model kestrel9b-int4h --port 9181 --no-autobatch
```
ci-bot: deploy-check: port 9181 up, eval queued.

anya: PROJ_READ_MODE=SOURCE reduces early-prefix L2 to ~1.9e-3 and rerank returns almost to baseline. Combining both fixes (alpha runtime + source proj read) makes results near fp16 baseline for most samples.

nick: actionable: 1) converter should expose --preserve-proj-order and a flag to not bake rotary alpha (alpha_mode=BINARY:BAKED|RUNTIME). 2) Add converter fingerprinting for proj-layout and tokenizer_normalizer in header to detect exporters that require preserve-mode. 3) Add eval guard that computes next-token logits L2 and softmax-KL over first 64 tokens and blocks onboarding if > thresholds.

dmitri: also add exporter checks: per-head quant scale outlier detection (fail export if head-scale > 8x median) and record per-head alpha quant stats. If alpha baked, warn if alpha quantization error > 1e-3.

anya: I'll open PRs: (A) converter add preserve flags + header fields (proj_layout_fingerprint, tokenizer_norm, alpha_mode), (B) add failing long-thread artifacts into /eval/artifacts/kestrel9b/ with token diffs and eval scripts.

sam: I'll add eval-side guards: L2>1e-3 or KL>5e-3 triggers triage.

nick: short-term mitigation in runtime: add a lightweight remap shim that can reorder packed proj slices on load if header mismatch; cheaper than re-exporting. Perf cost should be small.

anya: note: even after remap there's residual failure on threads with complex emoji/ZWJ sequences due to tokenizer norm mismatch. We'll need header-normalizer check and maybe recommend running tokenizer-alignment conversion step during onboarding.

ci-bot: ticket created: #ONB-4017 "Kestrel9b headwise-int4 rotary-alpha + proj-layout onboarding regression" assigned to anya/sam/dmitri, priority P2.

anya: uploading examples to /eval/artifacts/kestrel9b/ now and will link PRs. thanks everyone :thumbsup: 

sam: thanks, will follow up on the alpha quant prototype.

dmitri: ping me for pair on exporter fingerprinting and header schema.
